title: Annualization smoothing and usage escrow policy for large accounts
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Problem: Large enterprise customers experience high month-to-month usage volatility (training runs, seasonal spikes, product launches). At renewal this results in large true-up bills or unpredictable multi-year commit negotiations. That friction increases churn risk and drives discount pressure. Proposal: introduce two complementary contract primitives: 1) annualization smoothing: compute the baseline commitment for renewal using a weighted annualized average (configurable window, default trailing 12 months with quarterly weighting), and 2) usage escrow: a small percentage of committed spend is placed into a refundable credit escrow that buffers between committed and actual usage during the first 3 months post-renewal. The escrow can be consumed to cover overages before billing immediate true-ups and is reconciled quarterly. Goal: reduce sticker shock at renewals, preserve predictable revenue for Redwood, and offer customers a softer True-Up experience that reduces churn while enabling expansion motions.
motivation_and_context: Sales feedback and renewal loss analysis (Q1 2025–Q4 2025) show 18% of enterprise renewals had >30% usage variance vs prior year; of those, 42% reduced committed spend or requested steep discounts. Finance flagged recognition churn and collection risk when big true-ups invoiced. Ops reported multiple support tickets and delayed close. This feature aims to make renewals stickier and reduce discount-driven attrition while keeping revenue predictable via escrow treatment.
proposal_summary: 1) Annualization smoothing algorithm: baseline_commit = max(min_commit_floor, weighted_avg(trailing_12_months, weights=[0.5,0.2,0.15,0.15] by quarter)) with opt-out for customers who want month-level granularity. 2) Usage escrow: default 5% of committed ARR placed into an escrow ledger at renewal; escrow is refundable as credits for future usage or applied to true-ups over a 3-month smoothing window. Escrow can be captured as credit on the billing account; refunds only as account credit (no cash refunds). 3) Discount ladder: modest graduated uplift to next commit band when customers accept escrow (typical uplift 3–7% effective discount depending on term length).
pricing_examples: Example A - Customer has trailing 12-month billed tokens = $1,200,000. Weighted annualization results in baseline_commit = $1,080,000 (10% smoothing). If customer picks 3-year term with escrow=5%, escrow_amount = $54,000 held as credit. At quarter 1 post-renewal actual usage = $320,000 (vs q1 expected pro-rata $270,000), escrow covers $50,000 of overage; remaining $0 true-up invoiced to customer.

Example B - Customer with large seasonality: trailing 12 months $600k but recent 3 months spike to $400k. Weighted model yields baseline $520k. Escrow 5% ($26k) reduces immediate true-up; customer accepts 5% uplift discount for 2-year term, net effective annual price = baseline * 0.97.
acceptance_criteria: Legal approves conservative escrow contract language and clause for credit-only refunds
Billing system supports escrow ledger and quarterly reconciliation (ENG-2431 ticket created)
Finance confirms revenue recognition approach and approves for pilot customers (FIN-412)
Pilot signed with 3 anchor enterprise customers covering different profiles (seasonal retail, steady-saas, bursty-ml)
Telemetry dashboards show a 30% reduction in renewals with >20% true-up variance for pilot cohort over 12 months
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Design & Legal): finalize contract language; Phase 1 (Pilot 3 customers, 8–12 week pilot): engineering implement escrow ledger + reconciliation UI; finance validates revenue treatment; PM-run weekly pilot reviews; Phase 2 (selective GA): enable opt-in checkbox in renewal workflow, pricing sheet and CS playbook; Phase 3 (full GA): default offering for deals > $250k ARR with sales enablement and partner support.
metrics_and_signals: Average discount rate on renewals (target: reduce by 1–3 percentage points for pilot cohort)
Escrow utilization rate (percent of escrow consumed vs refunded)
Time to close renewal (target: reduce median by 10%)
Support tickets related to renewal disputes
decision_log: 2026-02-16: Decided weighted quarterly smoothing vs simple trailing mean to better reflect recent trends (trade-off: slightly more complexity in calculation).
2026-02-22: Finance prefers escrow as credit (no cash refunds) to simplify revenue recognition; legal to add clause preventing cash refund requests.
2026-02-27: Sales suggested optionality for customers to pick smoothing windows during negotiation; agreed to surface as 'opt-out' parameter in renewal sheet for flexibility.
2026-03-01: Chose default escrow percent 5% for pilot; adjustable by Sales on redline up to 10% with Finance approval.
open_questions: What is the GA threshold for allowing cash refunds vs credits? (Finance)
How to surface escrow balance in Redwood Console without exposing sensitive accounting fields? (Product/Eng)
Should we allow escrow to be funded by prior credits instead of require upfront payment?
Tax implications by jurisdiction for escrowed credits (Legal/Tax input required)
dependencies_detail: FIN-412: Revenue recognition approval + AR treatment
ENG-2431: Billing team to implement escrow ledger, reconciliation job, API endpoints, and a Console widget to show escrow balance
implementation_notes: Engineering estimate: 3 sprints to implement escrow ledger and reconciliation, 2 sprints for UI work in Console and Sales renewal flow. Minimum viable API: createEscrow(account_id, amount, term_months), applyEscrow(account_id, amount, reason), reconcileEscrowQuarter(account_id). Billing must persist escrow as liability ledger entry. Add audit logs and access control (RBAC) for ledger views. See Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIC/Annualization+Smoothing+and+Escrow+Spec and GitHub prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/4123
communication_and_docs: Customer-facing one-pager (draft) in Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/notes/annualization-escrow-onepager, internal CS playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/Escrow+and+Smoothing+Playbook , Sales pricing calculator spreadsheet: https://sheets.redwood.ai/d/pricing-escrow-calculator
risks_and_mitigations: Revenue recognition complexity: mitigation: run finance parallel tests on pilot and document treatment
Sales arbitrage / gaming: mitigation: limit opt-in escrow to negotiated deals and add guardrails in terms (no stacking of credits)
Operational overhead: mitigation: implement clear reconciliation automation and dashboards to reduce manual accounting work
